holidays.name: National Step in a Puddle and Splash Your Friends Day
holidays.description: Pull on your boots, find the nearest puddle and make a splash. Today is an official excuse to stomp around like a kid and get your friends a little wet. Dry socks are optional, but you'll probably want a spare pair.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and its creator is unclear. It has become a popular entry on fun-holiday calendars, a playful nudge to find joy in gloomy winter weather.
holidays.funFact: Puddle-jumping is more than child's play. Splashing in water is a classic kind of 'free play' that child-development experts say builds coordination and creativity.

holidays.name: National Milk Day
holidays.description: A day to raise a glass to one of the world's most familiar drinks. Pour a cold glass, dunk some cookies, or stir up a mug of cocoa. Milk goes with almost anything.
holidays.origin: It's commonly tied to January 11, 1878. On that date, milk is said to have been delivered in glass bottles to customers for the first time, in Brooklyn, New York. Dairy bottling then took off in the following decades.
holidays.funFact: Glass milk bottles changed how people bought milk. Before them, milk was often ladled from open cans into customers' own containers, so bottling made it much cleaner and safer.

holidays.name: Hot Toddy Day
holidays.description: A day to warm up with a steaming hot toddy in the middle of winter. It's a cozy mix of hot water, honey, lemon and a splash of whiskey or another spirit. Many people reach for one at the first sign of a winter chill.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It lands in mid-January, which is a fitting time for a warm drink.
holidays.funFact: The word 'toddy' may come from the Hindi word 'tari', which names a drink made from palm sap. Over time, the name came to mean a hot, sweetened spirit drink.
